PRE-SCHOOL
The Merlin School
Our Aim and EthosThe Merlin School, established in 1986, is a non-assessing pre-prep school for boys and girls, aged 3 – 8. You’ll find us in the heart of Putney, in a beautiful Victorian house. We specialise in educating children in these crucially important formative years and aim to ignite a life-long love of learning. There are two principal points of admission; children can join the Merlin Pre-School in the September after their third birthday or the Reception year of Main School after their fourth birthday.
Children at Merlin receive a broad and creative education, developing a thirst to learn within a supportive and inspiring environment, and each individual is encouraged to become independent and to have a go. Our aim at Merlin is to encourage a sense of excitement about learning, so every day is happy and rewarding. Above all, we believe that learning should be stimulating and confidence-building. There is a vibrant buzz about the school, where the children thrive as part of a caring community. Corridors and classrooms teem with life as we all work together. Our children leave Merlin superbly well prepared for the next stage of their school career. In a structured, supportive environment, we will lay the cornerstones of your child’s education.
Class sizes at Merlin are small, adult to child ratios high, and this enables us to nurture the children, helping every child reach their full potential. We’re proud of our Victorian school building with its many period features which lend a very special warm atmosphere. Our school hall, for example, used for assemblies, drama, music and dance, is the original ‘ballroom’. We teach in spacious classrooms in the main building and in three purpose-built cloistered classrooms at the rear of the school. For playtime, sports, and outdoor learning, there is a large playground, at the heart of the school and we go off-site for an afternoon of Games every week. Each of the light, airy classrooms is visually stimulating, with colourful, interactive displays and resources that are constantly updated.
At Merlin, our practical approach to learning enables the children to take an active role in every subject – they are never simply passive participants. English and Maths underpin our core curriculum teaching every day. Science, Music, Singing, PE, French and Computing are all taught by specialist teachers and we have dedicated teaching spaces for these subjects. This breathes life into the timetable and gives the children the opportunity to move around the school from lesson to lesson. Above all, the Merlin approach captures the children’s imagination, fires their enthusiasm and inspires them to want to learn. Through such creative and stimulating teaching of core, foundation and broader curriculum subjects, the children are well prepared at ages seven and eight for the next stage of their education in a broad range of the very best prep schools.
Insight into Merlin
Merlin BehaviourThe Merlin Behaviour Film aims to give parents an insight into how we manage behaviour here at Merlin as well as showcasing the Merlin spirit to a tee. Told though the eyes of the children, we hope you enjoy the film that was put together over the course of a typical academic year here at Merlin.
Themed DayOur annual Themed Day is a highlight of the Merlin calendar, where all year groups go ‘off-timetable’ and enjoy specially organised workshops, activities and sessions designed to ignite their love of learning and exercise those all-important skills and attributes so valued at our school, such as curiosity, creativity, problem-solving and collaboration. This year’s theme was ‘the power of play’ – have a look at the film for a sneak peek of the day.
Merlin School embeds a strong culture of Safeguarding.
To discuss any Safeguarding concerns, please contact the school or email dsl@merlinschool.net. If the school is closed and the matter is urgent, please email dsl@merlinschool.net.
Safeguarding mobile number: 07950166761

Why Merlin?

Welcome from the Headteacher
I am delighted to welcome you to Merlin School. Choosing a school for your child at the age of three or four is a significant decision and an exciting opportunity to inspire a young learner and prepare them for the next stage of their education. At Merlin, we specialise in these precious early years, providing a warm, nurturing, and homely environment that fosters confidence, curiosity, and resilience, alongside academic excellence.
The classrooms and corridors at Merlin are alive with happy learners working together and embracing challenges. Our children are supported, challenged, and inspired in an environment rich with opportunities and experiences. We pride ourselves on our personalised and practical approach to teaching, where each child is seen and valued as an individual. Small class sizes and a high adult-to-child ratio ensure that every learner makes excellent progress while developing a strong sense of kindness, respect, and independence.
At Merlin, the sense of teamwork is as strong among staff as it is between children. We work closely in partnership with families, supporting each one as they embark on their child’s educational journey. Choosing the best-fit next school after Merlin need not be daunting – each child is fully prepared and every family is guided and supported, helping to identify the environment in which their child will thrive. The children move on with confidence, enthusiasm, and a lifelong love of learning.
Merlin is a truly magical place, where curiosity and wonder abound, and each child’s talents are celebrated. I warmly invite you to visit and experience the unique atmosphere of Merlin for yourself.I look forward to welcoming you to our school.
A Message from the Principal
Having been involved in education since the 1990s, a great deal has changed during that time. Technology, and the impact that it has made on the world of work, has meant that schools and parents have had to re-think their ideas about the kinds of skills that children need to thrive in the future. Creativity, invention, collaboration, risk management and problem-solving are more important than ever in ensuring our children are being well prepared for their future.
I am delighted to be supporting the Merlin School with its onward journey, where pupils are given an outstanding education to discover and develop their talents and interests from such a young age.

After School Care & Clubs
Beams of Light Afterschool Care
Beams of Light is an Ofsted registered after school club run at Merlin School and is open to all Merlin pupils from Pre-School through to Year 3. They provide a variety of activities such as Home Economics, Drama, Design and Technology, ICT, tabletop games, Arts and Crafts and lots of outdoor physical activities.
Beams of Light After School Care runs on Monday – Thursday 3.30pm until 6pm, and on Fridays from 12.30pm until 6pm.
For more information, please see our FAQs.
NSSport Multi Sports (Year 1, 2 & 3)
NSSport is an externally run after school sports programme providing an active, safe place for our Year 1, 2 & 3 children to end their day at Merlin School. The aim is to provide a positive sporting experience for each child, whilst having fun. The sessions will challenge abilities and understanding within sport and support a healthy lifestyle.NSSport club runs on Tuesday afternoons from 3.30pm – 5pm.
Merlin Clubs
In addition to this, the school runs a broad selection of ‘Monday Clubs’ on a Monday afternoon and a Chess Club on a Wednesday afternoon for Upper School children.

French
French lessons at Merlin are fun, interactive and practical, full of songs and games. Children cover a variety of topics throughout their time at Merlin, from basic greetings, numbers and colours, to animals, body parts, weather, family, and food.
Children build an understanding of French culture as well as expression and styles of communication. The children are exposed to reading and writing a different and, for those who speak French at home, extension activities are personalised to those children by our native speaking French teacher.

Why Merlin?

Drama
Drama provides a forum in which to develop imagination and concentration, as well as the skills of communication and listening, movement and speech.Merlin children experience a rich variety of performances – from individual termly presentations to the class, our version of ‘Show and Tell’, to class assemblies performed to the school and parents, and full-blown musical productions in which each child has a speaking role. Original scripts have been adapted from sources such as Shakespeare, Tolkien, and the Greek myths, offering inspiration and challenge to the children.
Each year, children in Reception perform a Christmas Play in the Autumn Term, Year 1 perform a Spring Term production, and Years 2 and 3 perform their play in the Summer Term.
Recent productions have included The Canterbury Tales, Leonardo (The Life of Leonardo da Vinci) and Alice in Wonderland.

Why Merlin?

Science
Science at Merlin is fun and dynamic. Our curriculum supports a practical approach, with an emphasis on experiment and activity right from Reception. Making the connection between people and science is a fundamental part of our teaching. Science enhances the curriculum and provides a sound context through which to explore concepts.Science at Merlin
RECEPTION
Right from the word ‘go’ we immerse the children with investigations in Science. The Reception curriculum is very much based on practical sessions, with recording tasks in writing gradually introduced over the course of the year. Pupils are encouraged to observe in Science, in order to achieve the objective of getting them really excited about their learning. They investigate the world around them through topics such as the seasons, human senses, and the effects of heat and cold.
YEAR 1
Building on the Reception curriculum, the skills of scientific enquiry are further developed in Year 1 by including as many practical investigations as possible. Topics also encompass ‘Healthy Living’ themes and provide opportunities for the children to enjoy growing and studying plants.
YEAR 2
The principles of scientific enquiry continue to inform the Year 2 Science curriculum. Emphasis continues to lie in keeping the lessons as practical as possible. The importance of healthy living is reinforced along with investigations in new topics such as space and sound.
YEAR 3
Making the important connection between people and Science forms the basis of the Year 3 programme of study. The children continue to enjoy investigations and practical experiments. Pupils record their findings and use their observations to inform their opinions. Trips to London museums help support their learning.
Each year our Year 3 children enjoy a fantastic dissection lesson, generously led by one of our medically trained parents. This is a real highlight of the year and certainly one of the perks of being ‘top of the school’. Please see the video below for a glimpse into one of these special lessons.

Computing
Merlin has a dedicated computer suite in the cloistered classrooms and the children visit the specialist teacher once a week. The children learn a range of Computing skills during their time at Merlin. We start off with the basics, in Reception, learning how to use a mouse and a keyboard and progress to programming simple computer games using block programming languages like Scratch in Year 3.
We aim to deliver a vibrant, fun Computing curriculum to nurture the children’s love of technology but also remaining focused on keeping every child safe online, equipping them with the confidence to recognise when something doesn’t seem right and to seek help from a trusted adult. We expect every child to leave Merlin adept at using a computer at a basic level and with a desire to build on those skills outside of the classroom.

Why Merlin?

English
We encourage our children to explore their imagination and to express their ideas confidently, both orally and through creative writing. This goes hand in hand with promoting handwriting and the correct use of grammar and punctuation. We nurture a love of books at Merlin because we know that good reading skills will help the children progress in all other subjects.
The English language is vital for communicating in every aspect of our lives. At the Merlin School, we strive to develop a long-lasting enthusiasm for the written and spoken word. The ability to express ideas effectively, both verbally and on paper, is key not only to success in other subjects but also to developing self-esteem, confidence, reasoning and thinking.
At Merlin we enhance all children’s skills in reading, writing, speaking and listening, enabling them to express themselves with clarity, sharing dialogue and debate. We have a broad curriculum encompassing stories, poetry, drama and non-fiction. Moreover, we recognise that excellent expression in English requires assimilation of reading, writing, spelling, speaking and listening. It is these five main areas that form the basis of our English curriculum.
RECEPTION
Reading:Children read and understand simple sentences. They use phonic knowledge to understand regular words and read them aloud accurately. They also read some common irregular words. They demonstrate understanding when talking with others about what they have read.
Writing:Children use their phonic knowledge to write words in ways which match their spoken sounds. They also write some irregular common words. They write simple sentences which can be read by themselves and others. Some words are spelt correctly and others are phonetically plausible.Our curriculum is carefully differentiated to suit the needs of the individual child. The children are immersed in stories, spelling, phonics, language and reading in literacy lessons every day. As soon as the child is ready they are taught to write in cursive script.
YEAR 1
Speaking and listening is fundamental to the English curriculum; pupils are taught to speak clearly and to think about the needs of their listeners. A high standard of English is modelled constantly by staff both verbally and on paper and sessions regularly include shared reading and writing. Whilst phonic patterns and spellings become gradually more complicated, stories and creativity remain at the heart of our delivery of this subject.
UPPER SCHOOL – YEARS 2 & 3
We want all children at Merlin School to enjoy exposure to a rich and varied selection of books and nurture a real love of reading. Similarly, we aim to encourage children to develop a love for the written word, as well as acquiring the skills that will enable them to become imaginative and creative story-tellers.
Because accurate spelling supports Merlin children’s reading and writing, we ensure that our robust and differentiated spelling scheme helps them develop confidence with the phonic structure of language.
We teach children to understand inference in a text; they learn to recognize different styles of writing, including report writing, play writing, diaries and poetry. Requirements of the 7/8+ English curriculum are covered.

Why Merlin?

Mathematics
From number bonds to Euler diagrams, maths at Merlin is an exciting subject at all levels of ability. Our overriding aim is to ensure that the children master the core skills of maths, enabling them to become confident with numbers. Plenty of hands-on activities ensure that learning maths remains stimulating and engaging. Our priority is to ensure that our pupils grasp the fundamental aspects of maths, so that they have a solid foundation for building their skills and knowledge. Number bonds, multiplication tables and a variety of mental calculation methods are learned in order to develop this solid foundation.
We encourage pupils to be engaged, become active learners and show their ability to think, articulate and make connections wherever possible. We teach in a way that supports a depth of understanding, enabling children to make links between related concepts and to become confident and competent mathematicians. Mental maths skills are practised frequently; every maths lesson will start with a warm-up focused on this. Maths at Merlin is split into sessions covering strands such as numbers and the number system, shapes, space, measurement, calculation and handling data. Reasoning skills are embedded into the maths curriculum.
RECEPTION
We aim to promote enjoyment and enthusiasm for learning in maths, as well as confidence and competence with numbers and the number system. Children count reliably with numbers from 1 to 20 and are able to place them in order. They recognise numbers one more or one less than a given number. Using quantities and objects, they add and subtract two single-digit numbers, and count on or back to find the answer. They solve problems, including doubling, halving and sharing. Children use language to talk about size, weight, capacity, position, distance, time and money to compare quantities and objects and to solve problems. They recognise, create and describe patterns. Pupils can also explore everyday objects and shapes, using mathematical language to describe them.
YEAR 1
Pupils are helped to make calculations. They understand and appreciate relationships and patterns in number and space, as well as establishing their capacity to think logically and express themselves clearly. Their knowledge and understanding of maths is developed in a variety of ways, including practical activity, exploration and discussion. Children learn the 2, 3, 5, 10 and 11 times tables.
UPPER SCHOOL – YEARS 2 & 3
Our objective is to equip Merlin pupils with a range of mental and written methods (formal and informal). We develop their ability to solve problems, reason and make decisions. The ability to use and apply mathematics runs through all strands of maths teaching, and a problem-solving approach is sought wherever appropriate, rather than teaching it as a separate lesson. Children are expected to learn all their multiplication tables by the end of Year 3. We teach the 7/8+ syllabus within our lessons.
